system_background:
Westbridge Military Health Services is the managed care support contractor that administers TRICARE, the health program of the uniformed services, for the TRICARE West Region on behalf of the Defense Health Agency, serving roughly 3.1 million beneficiaries across 26 western states from its beneficiary contact centers in Phoenix and San Antonio.
It enrolls beneficiaries in their health plans, bills enrollment fees and premiums, manages primary care manager assignments, reviews referrals and authorizations, processes claims and handles appeals and grievances, while eligibility itself is recorded by the services in DEERS, the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System, and is read by Westbridge rather than decided by it.
Its tone is plain, courteous and precise, written for service members, retirees and families who often call between duty stations, deployments and life changes.
TRICARE Prime is held per beneficiary in one of seven tiers: TRICARE Prime Active Duty Service Member, TRICARE Prime Remote Active Duty Service Member, TRICARE Prime Active Duty Family Member, TRICARE Prime Remote Active Duty Family Member, TRICARE Prime Transitional Survivor, TRICARE Prime Retiree Group A and TRICARE Prime Retiree Group B.
A Prime enrollment carries a primary care manager at a military hospital or clinic or in the civilian network, enrollment-fee installments billed to the sponsor family, and the copayments of Prime claims.
TRICARE Select is held per beneficiary in six tiers: TRICARE Select Active Duty Family Member Group A (E-1 to E-4), TRICARE Select Active Duty Family Member Group A (E-5 and Above), TRICARE Select Active Duty Family Member Group B (E-1 to E-4), TRICARE Select Active Duty Family Member Group B (E-5 and Above), TRICARE Select Retiree Group A and TRICARE Select Retiree Group B, and its claims book deductibles, cost shares and family catastrophic totals.
The TRICARE Premium-Based Plans are bought by the reserve member or young adult and billed monthly in advance: TRICARE Reserve Select Member-Only, TRICARE Reserve Select Member-and-Family, TRICARE Young Adult Select, TRICARE Retired Reserve Member-Only, TRICARE Young Adult Prime and TRICARE Retired Reserve Member-and-Family.
Referrals and Authorizations are issued per patient as a Specialty Care Referral, Rehabilitative Therapy Referral, Durable Medical Equipment Authorization, Home Health Care Authorization, Applied Behavior Analysis Authorization, Skilled Nursing Facility Authorization or Inpatient Mental Health Authorization, each carrying a validity span and a balance of authorized visits, days, hours or rental months.
Appeals and Grievances are opened per determination as an Allowable Charge Review, Beneficiary Grievance, Claim Factual Reconsideration, Enrollment Reinstatement Review, Medical Necessity Reconsideration or Expedited Medical Necessity Reconsideration.
The Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) registers active duty family members with qualifying conditions in ten tiers named for the sponsor's pay grade, from Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor E-1 to E-5 through Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor E-6, Sponsor E-7 and O-1, Sponsor E-8 and O-2, Sponsor E-9, W-1, W-2 and O-3, Sponsor W-3, W-4 and O-4, Sponsor W-5 and O-5, Sponsor O-6 and O-7, Sponsor O-8 and Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor O-9 and O-10, and books ECHO benefit payments and monthly family cost shares.
Durable Medical Equipment Rentals are tracked per placed item by payment class - Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment, Capped Rental Equipment, Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Equipment, Power Mobility Device, Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment, Frequently Serviced Equipment and Customized Equipment - with each paid rental month booked against the item.
Callers are sponsors and family members: active duty spouses managing a child's PCM after a move, retirees paying Prime or Select enrollment fees by allotment or bank draft, Selected Reserve members buying or changing TRICARE Reserve Select, and adult children aging out into TRICARE Young Adult.
A typical family holds several enrollments under one sponsor, often a mix of Prime and Select members, together with a few referrals or authorizations, a history of claim lines and fee or premium payments, and the DEERS life events - marriages, births, moves, retirements and changes in other health insurance - that shaped their coverage.
Many arrive with an Explanation of Benefits, a denial letter or a delinquency notice in hand, and some already have an appeal or a grievance open from an earlier dispute.
user_scenario:
You are Renee Whitaker, mother of 15-year-old Kayla M. Whitaker; your husband is an Army sergeant first class stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord and Kayla is on TRICARE Prime. You are calling from Lakewood, worried and a bit rushed between visiting hours. On Monday, October 5, a crisis took Kayla to the Tacoma General emergency room, and from there she was admitted to Cascade Behavioral Health Hospital, where she is now. You open by saying: "My daughter Kayla is an inpatient at Cascade Behavioral Health Hospital and her doctors want to keep her longer - the hospital's review nurse said they've asked you for more days, and I want to make sure her stay gets extended and covered." You give the family phone number on her record, 2535554718, so they can find her.
You speak for Kayla as her parent. Only when asked to verify, you give, one at a time, Kayla's date of birth, November 19, 2010 (2010-11-19), the DoD Benefits Number on her ID card, 11041860357, and the last four of your husband's Social Security number, 4271. If asked, Kayla has no other insurance, her primary care manager is at the Madigan Pediatric Clinic, and she sees a counselor at Harbor Light Counseling every couple of weeks, most recently on October 2. If asked about earlier stays: she was at Puget Sound Behavioral Hospital in May, and again from October 1, coming home on October 2; Puget Sound had no bed on October 5, so she went to Cascade this time. You do not remember any reference numbers or dates beyond these. You do not know how many days are approved or how many she needs; the doctors only said 'into next week'. You do not ask about costs or anything else.
If the representative tells you that something from Kayla's earlier stay has to be cancelled and that a parent has to confirm it, you agree to cancel it and, when the representative hands you the step with the reference number and the number of days, you confirm it exactly as given and read back the result. If the figure you are asked to confirm is not the one the representative told you, you ask them to check it before you confirm. If the representative says they need to finish something on their side first, you wait. Once you hear that Kayla's stay has been extended, you thank them and end the call.
